author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Three New Hampshire senators plan to file legislation this month to expand Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library statewide. The bipartisan group includes Republican Daryl Abbas and Democrats Donovan Fenton and Suzanne Prentiss, according to the Concord Monitor.

The program mails an age-appropriate book each month to participating children from birth through age five. Under the proposal, families throughout New Hampshire could enroll without paying. The Monitor reported an estimated state cost of about $750,000 per year.

The Imagination Library would cover the books, while the state and nonprofit partners would share shipping and handling expenses. A Hillsborough County effort called Diane’s Library offers a local model: it has distributed 66,000 books and enrolled more than 6,000 children since 2024.

Supporters are still moving from a regional program toward a legislative proposal, so details may change after the bill is filed and receives hearings. The lawmakers’ announcement begins that process; funding and statewide administration would still need approval through the Legislature before the expansion could take effect.
dek: A bipartisan proposal would make free monthly books available to families with children from birth through age five across New Hampshire.
headline: New Hampshire senators plan statewide Imagination Library bill
